text: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace.
We always thank God for all of you, mentioning you in our prayers, constantly
remembering before our God and Father your work of faith, your labor of love, and your endurance born of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.

versions.text: remembering before our God and Father your work of faith, your labor of love, and your steadfast hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.
versions.explanation: ὑπομονή denotes active endurance under pressure; rendering the phrase as 'steadfast hope' collapses the triad's third member and loses the note of perseverance that parallels 'work' and 'labor.'

text: For we know, brothers and sisters loved by God, that he has chosen you.
For our gospel came to you not in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and with full conviction. You know how we lived among you for your sake,
and you became imitators of us and of the Lord, for you welcomed the word in the midst of great affliction with the joy of the Holy Spirit.
And so you became an example to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia.
For the word of the Lord has rung out from you, not only in Macedonia and Achaia; your faith in God has become known everywhere, so that we have no need to say anything.
For they themselves report about us what kind of welcome we received among you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God,

versions.text: They themselves tell us how we were welcomed among you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God,
versions.explanation: The Greek says they report concerning us (περὶ ἡμῶν) — that is, they tell others about Paul's team — not that they tell Paul. 'Tell us' reverses the direction of the report. The connective γάρ ('for'), which links this verse to the previous statement, is also unrepresented.

text: and to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead—Jesus, who rescues us from the wrath that is coming.
